reason: The prediction's own bridge undercuts its method clause. reasoning.given asserts 'Only an outside proxy reveals harness egress', and reasoning.landing narrows the resolution to 'an independent researcher, via published captured traffic'. Bridge validation.c2a6305a25854e90 (2026-07-16, rel=4) records xAI answering the wire-level teardown by open-sourcing the whole agent as xai-org/grok-build under Apache 2.0, and the bridge text says the effect directly: it 'hands researchers 844,530 lines showing exactly how a shipping agent wires uploads and permissions - an inspection template that lowers the cost of auditing rivals'. Source inspection is now a cheaper route to the same finding than a proxy capture, so the 'only an outside proxy' premise no longer holds and the landing clause excludes the method most likely to produce the next finding. Bridge validation.b1b0a2d8d1370b1b (2026-07-22) points the same way from the other side - Codex CLI's one-command import widens what a harness moves - while explicitly noting it 'is not the intercepted wire-level capture that would be a second finding'. Rewrite given and landing to admit source-derived disclosures, or state deliberately why they are excluded.
